title: Hills, Gears & Coasting
whatItIs: Hills change how your car speeds up and slows down. Use the right gear, and don't coast.
keyFacts: Coasting means rolling in neutral or with the clutch pressed down. Avoid it.
When you coast you lose engine braking, so you speed up quickly downhill and have less control.
On a steep downhill, choose a lower gear so engine braking helps control your speed.
Parking uphill: turn the wheels away from the kerb. Downhill: turn them towards it.
On single-track roads, give way to vehicles coming uphill whenever you can.

items.title: Going downhill
items.text: Use a lower gear so the engine helps you hold your speed.

items.title: Going uphill
items.text: You may need a lower gear. Hold back from slow vehicles ahead.

items.title: Coasting
items.text: No engine braking and less control. Keep the car in gear.

items.title: Narrow hill roads
items.text: Give way to vehicles coming uphill when you can.

a.label: Parked facing uphill
points: Wheels turned away from the kerb

onTheTest.question: Why is coasting downhill dangerous?
onTheTest.why: Coasting removes engine braking, so the car speeds up quickly downhill and you have less control.

traps: Coasting doesn't save useful fuel, and it costs you control.
Uphill parking: wheels away from the kerb, so the car rolls into it.
On narrow hill roads, the vehicle coming uphill usually gets priority.
